finding.claim: The allowlist check uses host.endswith("example.com") without a leading dot. ALLOWED_SUFFIX (".example.com") is defined at line 7 but never used. Any hostname that merely ends in the string example.com passes, e.g. attacker-controlled evilexample.com or notexample.com. The server then fetches an arbitrary URL on a host the attacker controls. That host can resolve to internal IPs such as 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1 or RFC1918 addresses. There is no scheme, port or resolved-IP check. The response length is returned, which gives a blind oracle for internal services.
finding.source: Query parameter `url` of GET /mirror (mirror.py:11), supplied by any unauthenticated client

trace.note: url taken directly from the query string
flawed endswith("example.com") check, no dot boundary
request issued to the full attacker-supplied URL

finding.guards_checked: Checked the hostname suffix check, which is bypassable via a domain like evilexample.com. The unused ALLOWED_SUFFIX constant is not applied. There is no IP or DNS-resolution validation, no scheme or port restriction, and no authentication. httpx does not follow redirects by default, so redirects are not an additional vector. The /ping endpoint uses a hardcoded URL and is not vulnerable.

verdict.guard_found: none (only host.endswith("example.com") at mirror.py:13, a suffix check without a dot boundary; ALLOWED_SUFFIX at line 7 is unused; no auth, middleware, scheme or IP checks)
